limitations: CloudBank Reference Estate is an official upstream reference application, not an attached customer system.
The projection is derived from a pinned static inventory and curated migration risks; CloudBank was not built or executed.
Oracle coupling is identified but no PostgreSQL or other target mapping is complete or selected.
Static source evidence does not prove application equivalence, migration completion, runtime behavior, or production readiness.
The fragment is bound to one exact canonical graph identity and fails closed after graph drift.

nodes.name: Cheque deposit and clearance risk 01: Transactional Event Queue

properties.statement: The workflow uses Oracle Transactional Event Queue/JMS configuration whose delivery contract requires a target messaging decision.

nodes.name: Cheque deposit and clearance risk 02: Delivery and replay

properties.statement: Deposit and clearance consumers must retain acknowledgement, retry, duplicate-delivery, and replay behavior.

nodes.name: Cheque deposit and clearance risk 03: Internal service authorization

properties.statement: Cheque consumers call protected account endpoints with service identity; database migration must not weaken that boundary.

nodes.name: Cheque deposit and clearance risk 04: Event-to-balance consistency

properties.statement: Pending journal creation and later clearance form an eventual-consistency contract that needs end-to-end comparison.

nodes.name: Credit score service risk 01: Nondeterministic output

properties.statement: SecureRandom output prevents literal response comparison and requires property-based acceptance bounds.

nodes.name: Credit score service risk 02: Date contract

properties.statement: The response uses LocalDate.now and therefore needs an explicit clock, timezone, and normalization policy.

nodes.name: Credit score service risk 03: API and security contract

properties.statement: The endpoint shape and CloudBank read scope remain part of equivalence even when no service-owned database table is migrated.

nodes.name: Credit score service risk 04: Operational equivalence

properties.statement: Health, metrics, traces, logging, failure propagation, and deployment behavior remain target acceptance concerns.

nodes.name: Customer and account management risk 01: Service-owned schema boundary

properties.statement: The account and customer services own separate Oracle schemas and Liquibase change logs; a target must preserve ownership and deployment order.

nodes.name: Customer and account management risk 02: Oracle identity generation

properties.statement: NUMBER identity columns with START WITH and CACHE semantics require an explicit target identity policy.

nodes.name: Customer and account management risk 03: Money and date semantics

properties.statement: Unscaled NUMBER balances and Oracle DATE/SYSDATE behavior require bounded precision, timezone, and default-value decisions.

nodes.name: Customer and account management risk 04: Constraint and ORM behavior

properties.statement: Primary keys, foreign keys, checks, uniqueness, JPA mappings, and repository queries must be compared at schema and API levels.

nodes.name: Authentication and service authorization risk 01: User repository schema

properties.statement: Oracle identity columns, VARCHAR2 character semantics, TIMESTAMP/SYSDATE defaults, uniqueness, and audit columns need target mappings.

nodes.name: Authentication and service authorization risk 02: Audit trigger semantics

properties.statement: An Oracle editionable trigger derives update identity through SYS_CONTEXT and REGEXP_SUBSTR; equivalent audit behavior must be designed explicitly.

nodes.name: Authentication and service authorization risk 03: OAuth scope boundary

properties.statement: APISIX and each service independently enforce CloudBank scopes; a database change cannot turn gateway checks into the only authorization layer.

nodes.name: Authentication and service authorization risk 04: Credential and secret posture

properties.statement: BCrypt hashes, database credentials, OAuth client secrets, and signing keys must retain their storage, rotation, and non-disclosure boundaries.

nodes.name: Money transfer risk 01: LRA coordination

properties.statement: The transfer service starts an Oracle MicroTx LRA and invokes account participants; the target must preserve coordination and termination semantics.

nodes.name: Money transfer risk 02: Compensation state machine

properties.statement: Complete, compensate, status, and after-LRA callbacks form a durable state machine that cannot be reduced to successful HTTP responses.

nodes.name: Money transfer risk 03: Local transaction boundaries

properties.statement: Participant callbacks combine distributed coordination with local Spring transactions and require atomic journal and balance behavior.

nodes.name: Money transfer risk 04: Journal idempotency

properties.statement: LRA identifiers and journal states must survive retries, duplicate callbacks, cancellation, and recovery without double application.
